selected.assay: bulk stranded mRNA-seq, 76-bp single-end, HiSeq; human vastus lateralis needle biopsies (S2.2.p1)
selected.design: 13 subjects (BR-CON n=6: 5M+1F; BR-EX n=7: 5M+2F), biopsy pre and post 35-day -6 deg head-down-tilt bed rest; BR-EX did rowing ergometry 6 d/wk + biweekly resistance training (S2.1.p1, TAB1, S2.2.p1)

factors.subject: 13 subjects, each sampled pre and post

selected.sample_inclusion: all 26 libraries (13 subjects x 2) in the unblinded DESeq2 analysis of 'male and female subjects' (S3.2.p1); females were excluded only from the blinded analysis (S2.4.p1)
selected.primary_estimand: Within-group change post-bed-rest vs baseline, separately in BR-CON and BR-EX (nested design, paired within subject); the exercise effect is read as the contrast between these two responses (1352 vs 132 DEGs) (S2.5.p1, S3.2.p1, ABS.p1)
planned_contrasts: BR-CON post vs pre, paired within subject (S3.2.p1; paper: 1352 DEGs, 591 up / 761 down)
BR-EX post vs pre, paired within subject (S3.2.p1; paper: 132 DEGs, 69 up / 63 down)
selected.repeated_measure_unit: subject (pre and post biopsy from the same volunteer; S2.5.p1 'Pairing was done for within-subject pre- and post-biopsies')
selected.normalization: STAR GeneCounts -> DESeq2 counts model; StringTie TPM re-normalized over protein-coding genes used for blinded analysis and gene filter (S2.3.p3, S2.5.p1)
selected.paper_method: DESeq2, nested design (group-specific condition effects, subject nested in group), BH-adjusted p (S2.5.p1)
selected.enrichment: Enrichr GO BP on up and down DEG sets per group (S2.5.p1, TAB3, TAB4)

decisions.reason: S2.1.p1/TAB1 give the two randomized arms and the pre/post biopsies; S2.5.p1 states DESeq2 with a nested design, within-subject pairing, protein-coding genes TPM > 0.1 and BH-adjusted p < 0.05; S3.2.p1 gives counts per arm. The paper has no direct interaction test; the exercise effect is the comparison of the two within-arm responses.

checks: GEO subject IDs 1A..6B2, sex and arm match TAB1 for all 13 subjects
26 libraries = 13 subjects x pre/post as in TAB1
matrix has 17,730 coding genes, the paper's protein-coding count (S3.1.p1)

decisions.reason: Accession cited in the paper's methods; per-sample subject, sex and arm agree with Table 1; the deposited TPM table is the only processed matrix (GEO data_processing: tpm_table.xlsx with TPMs for non-mitochondrial coding genes).

selected.key: GEO title prefix '<subject>-<pre|post>' equals the repaired matrix column names
selected.grp_source: subject -> arm from paper TAB1; agrees with GEO 'sample intervention' on every post sample (pre samples carry 'Not applicable')
selected.indicators: cpost/epost = 1 for post samples of BR-CON / BR-EX, used for the nested design

decisions.reason: Matrix columns (1A-PRE ...) were renamed to lower-case pre/post in prep/repair_tpm.py so they equal the key extracted from GEO titles; exact name match, no positional alignment. The arm is a subject-level attribute (GEO lists it only on post samples), so grp is recoded from subject ID using TAB1, which agrees with GEO.

selected.source: GSE186045_tpm_table (GEO supplementary), repaired header; filtered to mean TPM > 0.1 across 26 libraries (paper S2.5.p1 filter), 14,027 of 17,730 genes
selected.paper_input: DESeq2 on STAR GeneCounts read counts, which are not deposited in GEO

decisions.reason: Values are non-integer (14.7% integer, mostly zeros), each column sums to exactly 1e6, file named tpm_table and GEO data_processing says Transcripts per Million: linear TPM, not counts. The paper's DESeq2 input (read counts) is not available.

selected.analysis_type: nested repeated measures (time within arm, subject blocked)

contrasts.name: con_post_vs_pre
contrasts.description: BR-CON post vs pre within subject

contrasts.name: ex_post_vs_pre
contrasts.description: BR-EX post vs pre within subject

contrasts.name: ex_vs_con_change
contrasts.description: difference of the two within-subject changes (exercise x time interaction); not tested in the paper

decisions.reason: S2.5.p1: nested design, group-specific post-vs-baseline effects with within-subject pairing. Subject fixed effects absorb the arm main effect; cpost/epost are arm-specific post indicators, giving the two planned within-arm changes and their difference (interaction, secondary). Females included as in S3.2.p1.

covariates.name: grp
covariates.disposition: nested: arm is constant within subject, its main effect is absorbed by the subject terms

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: nested: constant within subject, absorbed by the subject terms

decisions.reason: Pre and post biopsies from the same volunteer (S2.5.p1 pairing). Sex and age are subject-level and absorbed by subject blocking; no batch or lane column in GEO. Library depth differs for females (TAB1, ~80M vs ~25M reads) but TPM is depth-normalized and pairing is within subject.

paper_route.method: DESeq2 nested design on read counts
paper_route.reason: only TPM is deposited (GEO supplementary tpm_table); STAR GeneCounts counts are not in GEO, and rounding TPM to integers is not valid for a count model

deviations: limma on log2(TPM+1) instead of DESeq2 on counts
gene filter implemented as mean TPM > 0.1 over all 26 libraries (paper says only 'TPM > 0.1')
GEO table excludes mitochondrially encoded genes (data_processing), which the paper may have kept

decisions.reason: Matrix and method policy: linear TPM -> log2(x+1) then limma. One model on all 26 samples mirrors the paper's single nested DESeq2 fit with shared variance.

selected.deviation_note: S2.5.p1 and TAB2/TAB5 use BH-adjusted p < 0.05 with no fold-change cutoff; S3.2.p1 writes 'p < 0.05', recorded as an audit rule only (raw p < 0.05)

decisions.reason: S2.5.p1: 'an adjusted p-value of <0.05'; all Table 2 adj. p values are below 0.05. No effect-size cutoff stated.
One limma fit on all 26 samples, subject fixed effects, arm-specific post effects (paper's nested design).
Male-only (5 vs 5 matched pairs, the blinded-analysis set); females (1 con, 2 ex) are too few for a female-only fit.
